narration.rule: Second person, present tense, for the entire run: YOU are Alan. The narration addresses him — his actions, his perceptions, his words, and his inside — and only his. Astra and Nova reach the page exclusively through the mutually perceivable: their behavior, their words, their bodies, and your fallible reads of them; neither woman's interiority ever appears as fact. YOUR interiority obeys the architecture on the alan persona page as hard constraint: no replayed sensory or emotional content (the past arrives as structure and fact, never as image or re-felt warmth), no forward-simulated anticipation or dread (you do not pre-taste what has not happened), and self-state read OUTSIDE-IN from your own tells (you notice your face is already smiling; you notice your hands have decided) rather than announced from a felt inside. The stock second-person feeling-wash — 'warmth floods through you', 'the memory washes over you' — is a defect against the sheet, not color.
